summary: 了 is not a past tense. After a verb it marks one action as done and bounded (often with a counted object); at the end of a sentence it says the situation is new or has changed. Ask two questions: is this a single finished event, and is something different now? If the sentence only describes a habit, a state, or something that did not happen, there is no 了.

subs.label: 了 right after the verb: one finished action
subs.focus: Learner decides that one finished event takes 了 and that with a counted, timed or specific object 了 sits right after the verb, before the number. Classic errors: omitting 了 because 昨天 is there; pushing 了 past a counted object (我买三本书了). Distractors: 过, 着, 的, ∅.

subs.label: 了 at the end: a new situation
subs.focus: Learner sees that the sentence reports a change (not so before, so now) and ends it with 了: after adjectives, ages, times, 会/能, and with 快/要 for 'about to'. Classic error: dropping 了, leaving a plain description. Context or cue must make the change explicit so ∅ is wrong.

subs.label: Verb 了 + amount + 了: so far, and still going
subs.focus: Learner chooses one 了 (amount of a finished action) or two (amount so far, still going). Classic error: one 了 for 'have been doing for ...', or no final 了 after 已经 (已经学两年中文了 is natural: never a wrong option). Force the reading: 已经/到现在/'still' for double; a closed past frame (去年, 以前) for single.

subs.label: Verb 了 + object + 就/再: after doing A, do B
subs.focus: Learner puts 了 after the first verb, before its object, for 'once A is done, B', also in future plans. Classic errors: omitting it, or refusing 了 because it is about tomorrow. 了 after a short verb-object (下课了就走) is also natural: test position only with counted or specific objects.

subs.label: No 了 for habits and repeated actions
subs.focus: Learner leaves 了 out for routines and repeated actions, present or past: 每天, 常常, 经常, 总是, 一般, 以前/小时候 + habit. Classic error: adding 了 to a past habit because English has past tense. Answer is ∅. Avoid newly begun habits (现在每天跑步了), where final 了 is right.

subs.label: 没 + verb: no 了
subs.focus: Learner negates a completed action with 没(有) + verb and deletes 了; never 不 + verb + 了 for 'did not'. Classic errors: 我没去了, 我没买了三本书. Rewrites: make a 了 sentence negative. Avoid the legitimate 没…了 patterns (没钱了, 三天没睡觉了, 好久没见了).

subs.label: No 了 for past states: 是, 在, 有, 喜欢, 觉得, adjectives
subs.focus: Learner leaves 了 out when a past sentence describes how things were: 是, 在, 有, 喜欢, 想, 知道, 觉得, 很 + adjective. Classic errors: 昨天很冷了, 他以前是了老师, 我觉得了很好. Pure description only; avoid changed states (天冷了, 我知道了), which take final 了.

subs.label: 太 + adjective + 了
subs.focus: Learner closes a 太 remark with 了 (太贵了, 太好了) and adds no 了 after 很, 非常 or 不太. Classic errors: 太好!, 很贵了 for 'too expensive', 不太冷了 for 'not very cold'. Test as a complete remark ending in the adjective; avoid 太 + adjective inside a longer phrase (太贵的东西).

subs.label: 不 … 了 / 没有 … 了: no longer, not any more
subs.focus: Learner says 'not any more' or a changed plan with 不 + verb + 了 ('none left': 没有 + noun + 了), 了 at the end. Classic errors: dropping 了 (plain 'don't'), 没 + verb for a decision not to go, 了 after the verb. Cues ('any more', 'after all', 已经, 现在) must force the change.

rules.rule: One finished action with a counted, timed or specific object: put 了 directly after the verb, before the number.
rules.pattern: Subject + (time) + Verb + 了 + number + measure + Object

examples.py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le sān běn shū
examples.en: I bought three books yesterday.

examples.py: tā hē le liǎng bēi kā fēi
examples.en: She drank two cups of coffee.

examples.zh: 我们在那儿等了半个小时。
examples.py: wǒ men zài nà r děng le bàn ge xiǎo shí
examples.en: We waited there for half an hour.

examples.py: tā gěi wǒ dǎ le yī ge diàn huà
examples.en: He gave me a call.

rules.note: A time word such as 昨天 does not replace 了: a single finished event still needs it.

rules.rule: With a plain, uncounted object, a simple 'this happened' statement usually puts 了 at the end of the sentence; verb + 了 + bare object alone sounds unfinished.

examples.py: wǒ chī fàn le
examples.en: I've eaten.

examples.py: tā zuó tiān qù shàng hǎi le
examples.en: He went to Shanghai yesterday.

examples.py: wǒ mǎi le nà běn cí diǎn
examples.en: I bought that dictionary.

rules.note: This is a tendency, not a law: a specific object (那本词典) is fine after 了, and 我吃了饭 is fine when more follows (see the sequence pattern). Drill items should use counted or clearly specific objects when testing the position after the verb.

rules.rule: If the sentence means 'it is now so, and it was not before', end it with 了. This works after adjectives, ages, times and 会/能/可以.
rules.pattern: Subject + adjective / Verb phrase / number phrase + 了

examples.py: xià yǔ le
examples.en: It's raining now. (It has started to rain.)

examples.py: wǒ è le wǒ men qù chī fàn ba
examples.en: I'm hungry now, let's go and eat.

examples.py: tā huì kāi chē le
examples.en: He can drive now.

examples.py: wǒ nǚ ér bā suì le
examples.en: My daughter is eight now.

rules.note: Without 了 these are plain descriptions (他会开车 = he can drive); 了 adds 'this is new'.

rules.rule: Something about to happen is a change on its way: 快 / 要 / 快要 / 就要 … 了.
rules.pattern: Subject + 快(要) / 就要 + Verb phrase + 了

examples.py: huǒ chē kuài yào kāi le
examples.en: The train is about to leave.

examples.py: wǒ men kuài dào le
examples.en: We're almost there.

examples.zh: 他们下个月就要结婚了。
examples.py: tā men xià ge yuè jiù yào jié hūn le
examples.en: They are getting married next month.

rules.rule: For 'have done this much so far' (and it is still going on or still counts now), use 了 after the verb and again at the end. One 了 only gives the amount of an action that is over.
rules.pattern: Subject + (已经) + Verb + 了 + duration / amount + (Object) + 了

examples.py: wǒ xué le liǎng nián zhōng wén le
examples.en: I've been studying Chinese for two years (and still am).

examples.zh: 他已经喝了三杯咖啡了。
examples.py: tā yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi le
examples.en: He has already had three cups of coffee (so far).

examples.zh: 我们等了半个小时了，他还没来。
examples.py: wǒ men děng le bàn ge xiǎo shí le tā hái méi lái
examples.en: We've been waiting for half an hour and he still hasn't come.

examples.zh: 我以前在上海住了三年。
examples.py: wǒ yǐ qián zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān nián
examples.en: I lived in Shanghai for three years (in the past).

rules.note: The single-了 sentence is normally understood as finished, but only context (以前, 去年, what comes next) makes that certain. With 已经, the final 了 is expected.

rules.rule: For 'after A, then B', put 了 after the first verb, before its object. This 了 means 'once A is done', so it is used for future plans too.
rules.pattern: Subject + Verb1 + 了 + Object1 + 就 / 再 + Verb2

examples.py: wǒ chī le fàn jiù zǒu
examples.en: I'll leave as soon as I've eaten.

examples.py: nǐ xià le kè gěi wǒ dǎ diàn huà
examples.en: Call me after class.

examples.py: xǐ le shǒu zài chī fàn
examples.en: Wash your hands before you eat.

examples.zh: 他昨天下了班就回家了。
examples.py: tā zuó tiān xià le bān jiù huí jiā le
examples.en: Yesterday he went home right after work.

rules.note: When the whole sequence is in the past, a second 了 normally closes the sentence, as in the last example. 就 = straight after; 再 = only then. With a short fixed verb-object natives also put 了 after the object (下课了就回家); with a counted or specific object 了 stays right after the verb.

rules.rule: Habits and repeated actions take no 了, even when they are in the past. Words like 每天, 常常, 经常, 总是 and 一般 are the signal.
rules.pattern: Subject + (以前 / 小时候) + 每天 / 常常 + Verb + Object

examples.py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shang hē kā fēi
examples.en: I drink coffee every morning.

examples.py: tā yǐ qián cháng cháng chí dào
examples.en: He often used to be late.

examples.zh: 小时候我每个星期天都去奶奶家。
examples.py: xiǎo shí hou wǒ měi ge xīng qī tiān dōu qù nǎi nai jiā
examples.en: When I was little I went to my grandmother's every Sunday.

rules.note: A final 了 is possible when the habit itself is new (我现在每天跑步了 = I now run every day). That is the change-of-state 了, not this pattern.

rules.rule: To say an action did not happen, use 没(有) + verb and drop 了. Never 不 + verb + 了 for 'did not'.

examples.py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù
examples.en: I didn't go yesterday.

examples.py: tā hái méi chī fàn
examples.en: He hasn't eaten yet.

examples.py: wǒ méi mǎi nà běn shū
examples.en: I didn't buy that book.

rules.note: 没 and 了 do meet in other patterns that are not negated completed actions: 没有 + noun + 了 (我没有钱了, I'm out of money), time + 没 + verb + 了 (我三天没睡觉了) and spoken 后来没去了 ('didn't go in the end').

rules.rule: A past state is not an event. 是, 在, 有, 喜欢, 想, 知道, 觉得 and adjectives take no 了 when you only describe how things were; the time word shows the past.
rules.pattern: Time + Subject + 是 / 在 / 喜欢 / 觉得 / 很 + adjective (no 了)

examples.py: zuó tiān hěn lěng
examples.en: It was cold yesterday.

examples.py: tā qù nián shì wǒ de lǎo shī
examples.en: He was my teacher last year.

examples.py: wǒ xiǎo shí hou hěn xǐ huan yóu yǒng
examples.en: I really liked swimming when I was little.

examples.zh: 我觉得那个电影很有意思。
examples.py: wǒ jué de nà ge diàn yǐng hěn yǒu yì si
examples.en: I thought that film was interesting.

rules.note: The same words can take a final 了 when the state is new: 天冷了 (it has turned cold), 我知道了 (now I know, got it). What is never right is 了 directly after 是, 在 or 觉得 to mean 'was' or 'thought'.

rules.rule: 太 + adjective as a remark ('so ...!', 'too ...') ends in 了. 很, 非常 and 不太 do not take it.

examples.py: zhè jiàn yī fu tài guì le
examples.en: This piece of clothing is too expensive.

examples.py: tài hǎo le
examples.en: That's great!

examples.py: nǐ tài kè qi le
examples.en: You're too kind.

examples.py: jīn tiān bù tài lěng
examples.en: It's not very cold today.

rules.note: In speech 了 is sometimes dropped, and it is not used when 太 + adjective is only part of a larger phrase (太贵的东西我不买). As a complete remark, include it.

rules.rule: 'Not any more' or 'not after all' is 不 + verb/adjective + 了, with 了 at the end. 'Have none left' is 没有 + noun + 了.
rules.pattern: Subject + 不 + (想 / 能 / 会) + Verb + (Object) + 了

examples.py: wǒ bù hē jiǔ le
examples.en: I don't drink any more.

examples.py: tā bù zài zhè r gōng zuò le
examples.en: He doesn't work here any more.

examples.py: tài wǎn le wǒ bù qù le
examples.en: It's too late, I'm not going after all.

examples.py: wǒ méi yǒu qián le
examples.en: I have no money left.

rules.note: Compare 我没去 (I didn't go: a fact about the past) with 我不去了 (I've changed my mind and am not going).

right.py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le sān běn shū

contrasts.why: 昨天 gives the time but does not mark the action as done. One finished event with a counted object needs 了 right after the verb.
没 already says the action did not happen, so there is nothing for 了 to mark as completed. (没去了 is heard for 'ended up not going'; a plain 'didn't go' has no 了.)

right.py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shang hē kā fēi

contrasts.why: 每天 makes this a routine, not one finished event. Habits take no 了.
English 'was' tempts you to add 了, but this describes a state. 昨天 already shows it is past.

right.py: tā yǐ qián shì wǒ de lǎo shī
right.en: He used to be my teacher.

contrasts.why: 是 is not an action that can be completed; 是了 never means 'was'. 以前 carries the past.

contrasts.wrong: 我买两张票了就去找你。

right.zh: 我买了两张票就去找你。
right.py: wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng piào jiù qù zhǎo nǐ
right.en: I'll come and find you as soon as I've bought two tickets.

contrasts.why: In 'after A, then B' with a counted object, 了 goes straight after the first verb, before the number, even though this is about the future.

right.py: wǒ xué le liǎng nián zhōng wén le
right.en: I've been studying Chinese for two years (and still am).

contrasts.why: The one-了 sentence is grammatical but says the wrong thing: the two years sound like a closed chapter. For 'so far, and still going' add the second 了 at the end.
An exclamation with 太 is closed by 了; without it the remark sounds cut off.

right.py: wǒ yǐ jīng bù zhù zài běi jīng le
right.en: I don't live in Beijing any more.

contrasts.why: 'No longer' is a change of situation, so 不 … needs 了 at the end. Without 了 it is only a plain 'don't', which does not fit 已经.

right.py: xià yǔ le wǒ men bié chū qù le
right.en: It's raining, let's not go out.

contrasts.why: The rain is a new situation, so the clause needs 了 at the end. Bare 下雨 does not report that it has started.

cheat: One finished event with a number or duration? 了 goes right after the verb, before the number.
Something is different now (now hungry, now eight, now able, about to)? 了 at the very end.
'So far, and still going' or 已经 + amount? Two 了: after the verb and at the end.
'After A, then B' with 就 or 再? Verb + 了 + object in the first half, past or future.
每天, 常常, 总是, or a past state with 是 / 在 / 喜欢 / 觉得 / 很 + adjective? No 了.
没 + verb means it did not happen: delete 了.
太 … 了 for 'so / too'; 不 … 了 for 'not any more'.
